stops.name: São Paulo: the faction born inside the prison system
stops.date_confidence: the early 1990s origin of the Primeiro Comando da Capital inside the São Paulo penitentiary system is carried in the verified pool as attested background to jair_bolsonaro.journey.json. No founding date, prison, or document was verified in this session, so 1993 is a placeholder inside the attested decade and the day defaults to 01. Canonical São Paulo pin inherited.
stops.campa: Inside the São Paulo penitentiary system the Primeiro Comando da Capital forms in the early 1990s, a prisoners' association that becomes the dominant criminal organisation in Brazil and then a wholesaler to every state that will take its terms. It does not conquer Bahia; it franchises there, through alliances with local groups who keep their own names. Years later the Bahian press will call the faction she leads an ally of the PCC and, later still, will call her its partner, sócia, in her own right.

stops.name: Vitória da Conquista: the city where the record begins
stops.date_confidence: gap, not event. No source reached gives a birth date, a birthplace, a family, or a year of entry into the trade. 2017 is the year of the first reachable mention of her under any name, and the date here is a file-opening marker rather than anything that happened on that day. Vitória da Conquista is attested as the base of her faction by the Se Ligue Bahia report of 27 March 2025.
stops.campa: Vitória da Conquista, the third city of Bahia, sits on the plateau where the BR-116 comes up from Minas and the roads to the coast branch east. It is the hub of the state's southwest and the base of the faction the press calls the Bonde do Neguinho. Jasiane Silva Teixeira runs its finances. No source reached in this session gives her birth date, her birthplace, her parents, or the year she entered the trade. Her file opens where the Secretaria de Segurança Pública opened it, which is the only place anyone has opened it.

stops.name: Salvador: the third woman in the Baralho do Crime
stops.date_confidence: 13 February 2017 is the publication date of the Mais Região item headlined that a faction leader is the third woman to enter the Baralho do Crime. The article body was not reached; the headline is the evidence. Whether the deck entry itself was made that week or earlier is not established. Salvador stands for the Secretaria de Segurança Pública, which publishes the deck; no building was pinned.
stops.campa: The Secretaria de Segurança Pública of Bahia publishes its Baralho do Crime, a deck of playing cards bearing the faces of the state's most wanted, and she is dealt into it. Mais Região reports her as the third woman ever placed in the deck. The instrument is borrowed from the United States invasion of Iraq, where a deck was printed so soldiers could recognise the Baath leadership. Bahia uses it to teach its own population to recognise its own. She is a face on a card before she is a name in any biography.
stops.quote: Líder de facção é a terceira mulher a entrar no Baralho do Crime

stops.name: Vitória da Conquista: the Dama de Copas

stops.campa: UOL runs her under the card she was dealt: Dama de Copas, Queen of Hearts, spreading terror in the south of Bahia. The suit is assigned by a police design office, not chosen, and it is the only title she holds that anybody prints without qualification. Around it the press stacks the others across eight years: maior traficante, homicida, sócia, primeira dama, líder, viúva, each arriving from a different document and none of them from her. The card is dealt in 2017; her first arrest comes two years later.

stops.name: Vitória da Conquista: four cases open

stops.campa: Four criminal proceedings stand against her in Bahia, for homicide and for drug trafficking. The count is reported by the Bahian press in 2025 as the standing tally and is never broken down into dates, victims, or courts in anything reached here. One of them concerns the death of a prison officer, over which G1 reports she has been convicted. The other three are a number in a sentence. A woman is called the largest trafficker in a state of fifteen million people on the strength of a total nobody itemises.

Police find her there, eleven hundred kilometres from Vitória da Conquista, in the state that houses her faction's business partner. Bahia looks for her and she is in São Paulo, and when Bahia looks for her again in January 2025 she will be in São Paulo again. The Bahian press has its headline by the following day.

stops.name: Salvador: the request to serve at home
stops.date_confidence: 3 October 2019 attested as the publication date of the Jornal Correio item reporting that she sought house arrest for want of structure in the prisons. The argument is reported as hers or her defence's; the headline does not distinguish, and the body was not reached.

The argument is not about her; it is about the Bahian penitentiary system, and it is made in a country where the dominant criminal organisation was founded by prisoners protesting exactly that condition. The request travels up through the courts over the next fortnight and is refused at the top. In the same week she is moved from the capital to the far interior.

stops.name: Juazeiro: transferred to the interior

The distance is the instrument. A faction leader is worth less to her organisation the further she is from it, and the Brazilian state has been moving inconvenient prisoners into the sertão since long before there were factions. She will spend five months there and walk out.

The phrase primeira dama do PCC is the paper's, not a court's, and it stands in unresolved tension both with Estadão's sócia, which implies partnership in her own right, and with the widow and ex-husband problem.
stops.campa: A Tarde, the oldest newspaper in Bahia, runs her the same day under three nouns: trafficker, killer, and first lady of the PCC. The third undoes the first two. A first lady holds her place by marriage; a trafficker and a killer hold theirs by act. The paper prints the contradiction as a list and does not notice it. Between the lawyer's ex-husband in 2019 and Estadão's widow in January, the press has now assigned her authority to a man in three separate ways inside six years.
